item.research_question: What are the thermal stability, phase transition temperatures, and microstructural evolution of the metastable intermetallic phases in the CoCrFeMo0.85Ni high-entropy alloy?
item.material_system: CoCrFeMo0.85Ni high-entropy alloy (gas atomized powder, nominal equimolar CoCrFeNi with 0.85 Mo)
item.processing_route: Gas atomization of high-purity Co, Cr, Fe, Mo, and Ni powders (approx. 24 µm); thermal analysis via DTA and DSC with 5 K/min heating/cooling cycles up to 1400 °C under Ar atmosphere; interrupted DTA at 900 °C; microstructural characterization via FEGSEM, EDX, and EBSD
item.test_conditions: Heating and cooling cycles at 5 K/min up to 1400 °C; interrupted heating at 900 °C; analysis of as-received powder, interrupted sample, and fully solidified sample
key_findings: Solidus and liquidus temperatures determined as 1323 °C and 1331 °C, respectively.
Phase transitions observed at 800 °C (exothermal formation of intermetallics) and 1212 °C (endothermic dissolution).
As-received powder exhibits fine alternating layers suggesting spinodal-like morphology with minor elemental segregation.
After full thermal cycles, a dendritic microstructure forms with a single-phase FCC matrix.
The FCC matrix is depleted in Mo (<1/3 of dendrite content) and enriched in Ni compared to the dendrite core.
Dendrite cores contain a tetragonal (Co, Cr, Fe)-rich phase (presumed σ) surrounded by a Mo-rich rhombohedral phase (presumed µ).
The precipitation window for the cooling curve is identified between 780 °C and 1200 °C.
CALPHAD predictions show a single FCC phase above 1280 °C, which disagrees with DTA-derived liquidus at 1331 °C.
item.mechanism: The formation of the FCC matrix is driven by high mixing entropy reducing Gibbs free energy. During solidification, Mo partitions to the liquid phase due to its high melting point and sluggish diffusion, segregating to interdendritic regions. The metastable phases (σ and µ) form via spinodal decomposition and compositional modulation driven by segregation, where Mo enrichment acts as a precursor state. The coexistence of σ and µ phases is attributed to cooperative diffusion and the order of elemental partitioning, with the µ phase growing at the periphery of the σ phase.
item.limitations: The CALPHAD method may require further assessment for the transition temperatures of intermetallic formation in this HEA. The stabilization of the σ phase is a gradual process that is too slow to be fully observed in the DTA experiments due to kinetic effects. The study notes that the interaction of metastable phases in powder form can be eliminated by high-temperature treatment, limiting the observation of certain short-term phenomena.
item.future_work: Further detailed thermal analysis should be performed to derive remaining thermodynamic properties such as partial pressure and activity. Additional investigation of intermetallic phases is needed to facilitate understanding of atomic arrangement and orientation for optimal HEA design.
quotes: Solidus and liquidus temperatures of CoCrFeMo0.85Ni were determined by differential thermal analysis as 1323 °C and 1331 °C, respectively.
The morphologies of two intermetallics show matrix-based tetragonal phases bordered by Mo-rich rhombohedral precipitates around their perimeter.

Mo segregation and particle precipitation also relaxed the lattice dilation. Ultimately, Mo-rich intermetallic tends to act as strengthening phase for property improvement when the incorporating Mo element remains at a relatively low level to CoCrFeNi matrix
